newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul panel mulls weakening Finance Ministry power.
newsitem.headline: Seoul panel mulls weakening Finance Ministry power.

text.p: A presidential panel examining financial reform in South Korea would propose curtailing the authority of the Finance Ministry, a statement by the panel said on Monday.

The Presidential Commission for Financial Reform said it would recommend unifying the three financial watchdogs -- the Office of Bank Supervision, the Securities Supervisory Board and the Insurance Supervisory Board.
It said the unified financial supervisory board should be under the direct control of the Prime Minister and that the president should grant ministerial rank to its head.
At present, heads of the supervisory agencies report to the finance and economy minister.

Analysts said the commission's plan was aimed at limiting the Finance Ministry's functions to policy-making. They said the ministry's current involvement in policy execution exerted too much influence over the economy.

The 31-member commission also described the duties of the central Bank of Korea as designing and implementing monetary and inflation policies and it recommended the central bank governor chair the Monetary Board, which decides monetary policies.
The finance minister now heads the board and recommends to the president five of nine board members.
The commission proposed a seven-member board, consisting of central bank officials and business and financial industry representatives. It excluded Finance Ministry officials from the board.
The commission was set up in January after President Kim Young-sam said he would push forward reform of the country's backward financial sector.
The commission is expected to formally present its proposals to the president by the end of May.
